name: Aesthetic Fluency
description: Processing ease generates positive affect: stimuli that are easy to process are liked more. Proposed mechanism in marketing, design, and art. Could reflect predictability signals or metacognitive fluency judgment.
key_references: Reber, R., Schwarz, N., & Winkielman, P. (2004). Processing fluency and aesthetic pleasure: Is beauty in the perceiver's processing experience? Personality and Social Psychology Review, 8(4), 364-382.

Winkielman, P., & Cacioppo, J. T. (2001). Mind at ease puts a smile on the face: Psychophysiological evidence that processing facilitation elicits positive affect. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 81(6), 989-1000.
empirical_evidence: Behavioral: repeated exposure increases liking (mere exposure). Stimuli with high perceptual fluency rated as more beautiful. Priming studies support fluency hypothesis. fMRI inconclusive; candidate regions (OFC, insula) engage in preference judgments but causality unclear. Alternative: confound with stimulus familiarity.
